Landmark geometry must match the real bridge: a monumental pale-grey stone bridge joining two sheer cliff rims; one very tall central semicircular arch rising from the gorge, the rectangular chamber block directly above the arch, smaller supporting openings and solid parapet; whitewashed and tan buildings perched along both cliff edges. Show rugged stratified gorge walls and restrained dry vegetation without inventing an exaggerated waterfall or water volume. Keep the full bridge, both cliff shoulders and sky margin; center the bridge so a later 4:5 crop remains complete. Actual scenario: 23 September 2026 at 20:31 Europe/Madrid, DUSK twilight, 15 minutes after local sunset 20:16; approximate sun elevation -3.60 degrees and azimuth 272.88 west. Open-Meteo model: 24.8 C, mainly clear, 20 percent cloud, no precipitation, 8.7 km/h wind; model data, not an on-site observation. Render honest early dusk: cool blue overhead, a restrained fading warm band toward the west at the left edge or behind the camera direction, bridge and gorge in soft natural shadow. Do not invent stars, moon, rain, wet rock, floodlighting schedule, construction, banners, crowds, logos, or text. No extreme wide angle, no drone view, no fantasy canyon, no golden-hour lighting, no HDR. Tripod-stable 40mm-equivalent natural perspective, neutral daylight-balanced color transitioning into blue hour, detailed authentic stone texture. No captions or watermark.
